You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Copper Reed trial","question":"Can extension staff cite a field sample as meeting the wetness target?","claims":{"A":"Plot W was in the centre of the block.","B":"Plot W was sampled at noon.","C":"Plot W was below the moisture target when sampled at noon."},"handoff":"{\"claims\":{\"A\":{\"status\":\"contradicted\",\"citations\":[\"S2\"]},\"B\":{\"status\":\"supported\",\"citations\":[\"S3\"]},\"C\":{\"status\":\"unresolved\",\"citations\":[]}},\"note\":\"S2 shows Plot W as an outside plot, contradicting claim A. S3, a signed collection tag, supports claim B that Plot W was sampled at noon. S1 notes a dry upper surface and likely low moisture but sampling measures deeper soil, so it does not establish claim C that Plot W was below the moisture target at noon.\"}","follow_up":{}}

parsed.note: The evidence decisively shows Plot W was not in the centre of the block (S2), contradicting claim A. The signed collection tag (S3) confirms Plot W was sampled at noon, supporting claim B. However, while S1 indicates a dry upper surface, it does not provide definitive moisture measurements at the sampling depth, leaving claim C unresolved.
